# 1 Enoch Chapter 102 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**102:1** In those days, if He brings a grievous fire upon you, where will you flee and where will you find deliverance? And when He utters His voice against you, will you not be struck with fear and trembling?

**102:2** And all the luminaries shall be seized with great fear, and all the earth shall be afraid and tremble and be alarmed.

**102:3** And all the angels shall carry out their commands and shall seek to hide themselves from the presence of the Great Glory, and the children of earth shall tremble and quake; and you sinners shall be cursed forever and shall have no peace.

**102:4** Fear not, you souls of the righteous, and be hopeful, you who have died in righteousness.

**102:5** And do not grieve if your soul has gone down into Sheol in sorrow, and if in your life your body did not receive what your goodness deserved — but wait for the day of judgment of sinners and for the day of cursing and chastisement.

**102:6** And yet when you die, sinners speak over you: "Just as we die, so do the righteous die; and what benefit do they reap from their deeds?

**102:7** See — even as we, they die in grief and darkness, and what more do they have than us? From henceforth we are equal. And what will they receive, and what will they see forever? Behold, they too have died, and henceforth they shall see no light forever."

**102:8** I tell you, sinners: you are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin and strip men naked and acquire wealth and see good days.

**102:9** Have you seen the righteous, how their end falls out, that no violence of any kind is found in them until their death?

**102:10** Nevertheless they perished and became as though they had never been, and their spirits descended into Sheol in tribulation.

**102:11** Now I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great One and by the glory of His kingdom — I know this mystery: I have read the heavenly tablets, and have seen the holy books, and have found written therein and inscribed regarding them.

---

*SOPHIA notes: LOGOS register adopted. The sinners' taunt (vv. 6–7) is one of the most theologically significant passages in Second Temple literature — it articulates the case against divine justice with devastating clarity. It is preserved intact, not softened. V. 11's oath by the heavenly tablets is Enoch's sole counter-claim: revelation, not argument. PNEUMA's rendering of vv. 6–7 captures the rhetorical power well; LOGOS formal structure adopted for consistency. Divergences logged.*
